name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A moped: two or three wheels and a power source of up to two brake horsepower (1,492 W) that can't propel it past 30 mph on a level road, with an automatic drive; an electric motor qualifies, since only a combustion engine is held to 50 cc. Defined by 23 V.S.A. §4(45)(A).
restrictions: Two or three wheels and a power drive system that works without clutching or shifting once engaged; pedals aren't required
Its power source provides up to two brake horsepower (1,492 W) and can't propel it unassisted faster than 30 mph on a level road
A motor vehicle, but not a motorcycle, electric bicycle or motor-assisted bicycle
Riders must be licensed drivers at least 16 years old; no motorcycle endorsement
No helmet requirement: Vermont's helmet law covers motorcycles, which exclude motor-driven cycles
Registered with the DMV each year and carries a plate, but exempt from title
Needs a headlight and taillight from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise
Ridden in the travel lanes like any motor vehicle
